---
title: RNAcentral
description: RNAcentral's id_mapping landed whole, and the non-coding RNA cross-references OrgDb lacks, derived for human and mouse.
---

[RNAcentral](https://rnacentral.org) aggregates non-coding RNA sequences: one
`URS` id per distinct sequence, cross-referenced to the records of its member
databases (ENA, Rfam, Ensembl, RefSeq, miRBase, HGNC, GtRNAdb and more). The
release lands `id_mapping.tsv.gz` whole, one row per cross-reference across
every taxon, and derives `annotation.rnacentral__rna` (one row per sequence
per organism, with its RNA type) and RNAcentral's rows in
`annotation.identifier_mapping`. The release number is the version.

## Licence and citation

CC0 1.0 (from release 20). Cite RNAcentral as
[its site asks](https://rnacentral.org/about-us), with the release number.

## Join keys

- The id is the taxon-qualified `URS0000626831_9606` (`urs_taxid`), not the bare `URS`: a sequence occurs in many organisms. HGNC's `rna_central_id` is the bare form, so the join is `|| '_9606'`.
- `annotation.identifier_mapping` rows under `source = 'RNACENTRAL'` use the member database names as target namespaces (`HGNC`, `MIRBASE`, `RFAM`, `REFSEQ_RNA`, `ENSEMBL_TRANSCRIPT`), the forms NCBI and MANE already write.
- `taxon_id` joins every gene table.

## Good to know

- The derived tables cover human and mouse so far; raw covers every taxon.
- ENA composite ids (`GU786683.1:1..200:rRNA`) are kept as published in raw and are most of the rows.
- RNAcentral's Ensembl ids are transcripts, so they land under `ENSEMBL_TRANSCRIPT`, not `ENSEMBL`.
